newsitem.title: USA: USDA says US soy acreage may be highest since 1984.
newsitem.headline: USDA says US soy acreage may be highest since 1984.

text.p: U.S. soybean acreage this year could top 65 million acres, the highest since 1984, the Agriculture Department's chief economist said Monday.

Boosted by current favorable prices, Keith Collins said that 1997/98 soybean plantings could reach 64.5 million acres, "or even exceed 65 million." He said soybean output could total 2.5 billion bushels, and stocks could rise to 220 million.

Speaking at USDA's annual Agricultural Outlook Forum, Collins also projected 97/98 U.S. corn acreage at 81 million acres, down 500,000 acres from the baseline projection the agency used in developing the budget.
Collins said U.S. corn production this year could total "close to 9.6 billion bushels," the second highest ever, and that stocks could rise to more than 1.2 billion bushels.
U.S. wheat acreage will drop slightly this year, Collins said, due to a seven percent decline in winter wheat acreage and lower price expectations than a year ago for spring wheat plantings.
He projected this year's wheat crop at 2.28 billion bushels, the same as last year, but below 97/98 baseline projections of 2.345 billion bushels. Wheat stocks could rise to 550 million bushels.

Collins said U.S. crops will see strong export competition from large competitor supplies stemming from good crops last year. But he noted that smaller crops are expected in all the major competing exporters except the EU, and that this "should provide an opportunity for a recovery in U.S. exports."
